land.text: British Burma, the last shape of Cliopatria's British Raj row (1947, 748,070 km2), which holds 2,261 Myanmar cells

predecessors.note: The Independence Act is dated 10 December 1947, and the state was established on 4 January 1948 (Union of Burma page). Cliopatria's British Raj row still contains Burma in 1947, though the Raj itself ended in August 1947; the British-Indian side of 1947 belongs to the India and Pakistan dossiers.

capitals.name: Rangoon (Yangon)
capitals.note: Capital: Rangoon. The military moved the capital in November 2005.

capitals.name: Naypyidaw
capitals.note: The military moved the capital from Yangon in November 2005. On 27 March 2006, the junta officially named the new capital Naypyidaw.

keyframe_review.note: 675,942 km2 against the infobox's 676,579 km2 (ratio 1.00), so the area is right; the outline is not: it is the Konbaung outline of 1819 (2,333 cells against 2,334) reused for the republic, with 71 cells in Thailand, China and Laos and 35 cells of Myanmar missing. The correction is the modern country; the Union of Burma page gives no boundary and no area.

region.text: Burma, the land of today's Myanmar

ledger.note: 1948: Burma becomes an independent republic on 4 January 1948. 'On 4 January 1948, the nation became an independent republic, under the terms of the Burma Independence Act 1947' (Myanmar page); the Union of Burma page gives the Independence Act as 10 December 1947 and the capital as Rangoon. The pages name the country, not a boundary.

1962: General Ne Win seizes power on 2 March 1962, arresting U Nu and declaring a socialist state under the Union Revolutionary Council; the state, its name and its borders continue (the Burma Socialist Programme Party was founded on 4 July 1962).
1974: the Socialist Republic of the Union of Burma. 'A new constitution of the Socialist Republic of the Union of Burma was adopted in 1974.'
1989: Burma becomes the Union of Myanmar. 'SLORC changed the country's official English name' to Union of Myanmar on 18 June 1989, after the coup of 18 September 1988 (infobox) that formed the SLORC.
2005: the capital moves from Yangon to the new city later named Naypyidaw (The military moved the capital from Yangon in November 2005; named on 27 March 2006).

wars.name: Internal conflict in Myanmar
wars.outcome: No border change: Communist and ethnic insurgencies affected the early years, including the Karen National Union; after 1949 a Kuomintang army controlled remote areas of northern Burma. The ethnic and insurgent-held zones are not drawn as territory of other states.
wars.note: The pages opened date no insurgent-held zone, so none is recorded as an occupation or a contest.

certainty.note: The international frontier of a modern state (the Myanmar page gives a 2,185 km border with China and borders with Bangladesh, India, Laos and Thailand), though no page opened dates the border agreements; insurgent-held interior zones are not drawn.

notes: SPLIT of the Cliopatria Name 'Burma' (1820..1989): the 1948-1989 shapes (burma_1948, burma_1987) belong to this dossier, together with the Union of Myanmar row (1990..2024), which shares Wikidata Q836; they are one state (Union of Burma, renamed Union of Myanmar on 18 June 1989). The 1820-1884 shapes are the Konbaung kingdom, dossier 'burma'. The slug 'union-of-burma' is new (slugify of the name); the se-04 group lists union-of-myanmar as its own row with a 1-2 page budget and should not write a second dossier for those two shapes, or should cite this one. Cliopatria errors found: the 1948-2024 outline is the Konbaung outline of 1819 reused (71 cells outside modern Myanmar, 35 missing inside). Page silent: the Union of Burma page has no area, no boundary and no Frontier Areas or Panglong text; no border agreement date (China, Thailand, India, Bangladesh, Laos) appears on either page; the Kuomintang army controlled remote areas of northern Burma after 1949 without dates; the Shan Sawbwas lost their powers in 1959; the 2010 name change to the Republic of the Union of Myanmar is not on the Myanmar page. Not recorded as territory: the Kuomintang-held zones, insurgent-held zones, the 2021 coup. Counterparts needing dossiers: Karen National Union and the Communist Party of Burma (insurgent states, not drawn), the Kuomintang army in northern Burma. Budget: 2 pages (Union of Burma, Myanmar) for 4 shapes. Quote policy: single quotation marks enclose only wording that the WebFetch result itself gave in quotation marks; every other statement attributed to a page is a close paraphrase.
